purpose: Which real BMW sources could supply demo data: real configurations with codes, and the shape of real new-car stock.

stockLocator.access: Public: no API key, no login; plain HTTPS with a session cookie. robots.txt has no Disallow rules.
stockLocator.modelList: 60 selectable models on the start page, each with data-modelno, data-series and data-body.
stockLocator.searchRequest: GET /results?f=..&v[vehicle_ids][]={modelno}&p=..&ds=..&d=..&min=..&max=..&debug=.. (scalar values Base64-encoded by the page script)
stockLocator.paging: 10 cars per response; the page calls ./results/more until finished=true.
stockLocator.responseShape: JSON object { location: [car], filters, sortBy, finished }
stockLocator.noCodes: No model code, AG code or option codes anywhere in the results or vehicle detail page; options are display titles only.
stockLocator.detailRoute: /vehicle/{encrypted vin}/{iv}?dn={dealer}&f={finance}: server-rendered page with technical data.
stockLocator.notRetained: No order numbers, VINs, dealer IDs, prices, image URLs or response bodies are kept in this file.

configuratorVssCode.request: POST /similarity-search/v2/search with searchContext.vssConfigurationId = agModelCode + ':' + sorted normalised option codes joined by ','
configuratorVssCode.normalisedOptions: Option elements only (accessories excluded), using the base code rather than any combined code
configuratorVssCode.encoding: No Base64 in the request body as built by the page
configuratorVssCode.liveStatus: Not observed: the UK settings have VSS.enable=false, so the call did not fire in a headless page load.
